data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Graph coloring impossibility is a global topological property; the tensor parity argument operates entry-wise and the global coupling is through shared rank-1 terms.","Odd cycle non-2-colorability is a theorem; the ternary rank-22 non-existence is a conjecture that may fail due to richer combinatorial structure.","Graphs have well-understood parity; tensor entries interact through 18 input variables, making the parity coupling far more complex."],"overturn_conditions":["A ternary rank-22 decomposition is explicitly found, collapsing the analogy.","The parity argument is shown inapplicable because zero tensor entries absorb parity mismatches.","Exhaustive search over ternary rank-22 is shown computationally infeasible, so the obstruction is untestable at this scale."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a discrete structure (odd cycle / tensor entry pattern) where a parity constraint on the number of available resources (colors / rank-1 terms) creates an impossibility.","Both have a natural 'one more resource' solution: 3 colors for any graph / 23 terms for the tensor.","Both are decidable by exhaustive combinatorial search within a bounded class."],"source_memory_refs":["parity_coloring_obstruction"],"transfer_claims":["If the parity obstruction holds for ternary <3,3,3>, then analogous parity obstructions may govern ternary-restricted rank for other tensor formats <n,n,n> where the minimal rank and the tensor entry count have mismatched parity.","The 'one more term' pattern (like 'one more color') may generalize: minimal ternary rank for <n,n,n> is constrained by parity of r relative to entry structure."]},"claim":"No rank-22 decomposition of the <3,3,3> tensor exists with all coefficient-matrix entries drawn from {-1, 0, 1}. The minimum rank achievable in this ternary-restricted class is 23, matching Laderman's construction. Consequently, if R(3,3,3) < 23, any rank-22 decomposition must use at least one coefficient with absolute value \u2265 2 or require non-integer entries.","counterconditions":[{"case":"An explicit rank-22 decomposition with all entries in {-1,0,1} is found and verified by the 729-entry integer check.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A constrained search over ternary rank-22 decompositions terminates without exhaustion (e.g., by pruning bounds that are too aggressive), so non-existence is not actually proved.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A rank-22 decomposition using coefficients in {-2,-1,0,1,2} is found, weakening the ternary-specific claim but not the broader structural parity argument.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The parity argument is shown to be flawed because tensor entries with value 0 can absorb parity mismatches, so the odd/even distinction does not propagate as claimed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A rank-22 decomposition is found over a small finite field (e.g., GF(3)) where ternary entries are natural, contradicting the claim even in the restricted setting.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The <3,3,3> tensor has 729 entries, each of which must be expressed as a sum of exactly r rank-1 outer-product contributions. With ternary entries, each rank-1 term contributes to a tensor entry a product u*v*w where u,v,w \u2208 {-1,0,1}, so each contribution is also in {-1,0,1}. For a tensor entry that equals 1, one needs an odd number of +1 contributions minus an odd number of -1 contributions from the r terms. With r=22 (even), the parity structure of the 729 target entries imposes combinatorial constraints: entries requiring an odd number of nonzero contributions face a parity mismatch if all 22 terms are active at that entry, forcing some terms to contribute zero at certain entries. This zero-forcing creates a graph-coloring-like constraint across the 729 entries whose satisfiability with 22 ternary terms is structurally blocked, analogous to how 2-coloring an odd cycle fails. The Laderman 23-term solution sidesteps this because 23 is odd, allowing natural parity coverage.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
